text:
A certain lady at a balcony, with stocking and tight slipper, stirred the limp asparagus of a rough peasant spying on her.


When she noticed his gaze, she asked its cause; the peasant opened his heart and told what he saw and contemplated.


Raising an eyebrow, she said coyly, “Brother, this is merely seeing and desiring the fruit.”


The peasant drew out his tackle, took it in hand, and replied, “Then see and desire, madam whore!”

translation.title: On a Certain Lady at a Balcony
